relevance_note: A literature review that summarises HA20 patients mostly at group level but also describes a few previously published patients individually, e.g. 'The second case was a 6-year-old Japanese boy.'
method_note: Read the whole review by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans/fields (no table transcription). Scope: the review summarises 74 East Asian and 51 other-region HA20 patients only at group level (Table 1); those get no rows. Rows were made only for previously published people the text describes individually: the two allogeneic-HCT boys ('The first case ... 14-year-old English boy', 'The second case ... 6-year-old Japanese boy'), the East Asian patient with Hodgkin lymphoma (10), the autologous-HCT patient with CNS vasculitis (30), and the one East Asian patient with elevated ISG expression (47). Labels follow rule 4 using the reference as printed; the two boys share the joint citation '(31, 47)' and are numbered in the order of their individual description ('first case' = English boy). The paper never assigns 31 or 47 to a specific boy, so '(31, 47)' is recorded for both; the text implies (not stated) that the Japanese boy is the single East Asian canakinumab/anti-IL-1 patient cited as (47) ('Only one patient was treated with anti-IL-1 agents (canakinumab) in East Asia (47)'), so that mention was treated as the same person and not given a separate row. The ISG patient (47) may also be the Japanese boy but the paper does not say so, so it has its own row ('ref (47) patient'); a reconciler should check. Ages '14-year-old'/'6-year-old' are the ages given in the case summaries (apparently around HCT) and were put in age_at_last_evaluation. Variant rows: the review says its patients have 'HA20 resulting from TNFAIP3 mutations' and shows East Asian mutations only in Figure 1, so each in-scope person has a TNFAIP3 row with variant_original_string 'not reported'. Variants named in the text (Cys243Tyr (45), Glu192Lys (18), Met476Ile (20), Arg183X (22, 27), Arg87X (21, 42), p.Asn102Ser, c.487-1G>A, p.Val309dup, Phe127Cys) are tied to references or families, not to identifiable individuals, so they were not attributed. Checklist judgements: 'insulin-dependent DM' -> type 1 diabetes observed; 'psoriasis' -> skin lesions observed; 'frequent fever' -> recurrent fever observed; 'hepatitis', 'enteropathy', 'cell depletion', 'bowel disease' and 'Hodgkin lymphoma' were NOT mapped to autoimmune hepatitis, GI inflammation, autoimmune cytopenia or lymphoproliferation (left not reported) because the paper does not specify them further. No exclusions were recorded; Table 1 counts are unnamed group counts. n_patients_reported = 125 is the sum of the two stated regional totals (74 + 51); no single total is printed, so cohort_size_as_stated is null. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: Table 1 prints '42/51 (82.6%)' (42/51 = 82.4%); the text says onset 'ranged from neonatal to around 30 years' while Table 1 gives 'neonatal period to 32 y'; the text says 'four potential splice site mutations or duplication mutations' then 'One ... in Japan (16), while four were reported in China (25, 27)' (1 + 4 = 5); allogeneic HCT is cited '(31, 47)' after 'one refractory patient in East Asia and one refractory patient in other regions', which by order would map 31 to East Asia, unlike the inference above.
